speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether there are plans to elevate the role of nutrition in managing diabetes and pre-diabetes; and (b) what is the percentage of people who have utilised the Diabetes Risk Assessment Tool since its inception and found to be at risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Good nutrition involves having a healthy and balanced diet that is lower in sugar, saturated fat and calories, and higher in whole grains, fruits and vegetables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It also includes other lifestyle changes, such as exercise and weight management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The aim is to encourage more food innovation to widen the HCS range.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Just recently, Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin and I were at Singapore Polytechnic to look at some of the new products that the industry has developed, including the use of resistant starch, beta glucan, to help lower the glycemic index of staple foods like noodles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Besides a healthier diet, prevention and management of diabetes also involve adopting an active lifestyle, going for appropriate health screening and follow-up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The national screening programme Screen For Life run by HPB aims to improve early detection and appropriate intervention of chronic diseases, including diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Similar tools have been implemented in countries, such as the United Kingdom, Australia and the United States.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Those who are assessed to be at higher risk will be advised to go for diabetes screening and follow-up consultations with doctors.
